title: Rafael Gorski — Agents are software. Build them like it.
description: Rafael Gorski on building agents and AI systems, told as a climb: the route from the first decision to accountable operation, the valleys where teams stall, the gear to carry and his trail log, with every point linked to its evidence.
thesis: Agents are software. Build them like it.
lede: Launching and scaling an AI system is a climb. I build agents and the software around them, and I work with teams the way a mountain guide does: walk the route with them, name the valleys before we reach them, and check the gear at every camp.

who.label: Paper
who.text: [Problem-Based Software Requirements Specification](https://doi.org/10.21529/RESI.2016.1502002), with Paulo Cézar Stadzisz, 2016

own: Views are my own, not my employer's.

take.heading: How I lead a climb
take.intro: What I hold to when building agents and the systems around them, with the evidence beside each point.

positions.title: Start from the problem, not the model.
positions.body: A model can't fix a problem nobody wrote down. I start with who has the problem, what it costs them and how we'll know it's solved. Then every feature has to trace back to it. Agents make this matter more, because they will happily build what nobody asked for.
positions.say: My own method sits in Trial on the radar, not Adopt. One paper and one open-source skill are not settled evidence.

positions.title: Evaluations are the spec you can run.
positions.body: I don't trust a prompt, skill or model change I can't test. Deterministic checks run on every push. A model grading outputs earns trust only after it agrees with people grading the same ones. A benchmark score says a model managed someone else's task once, not that my system will, every time.
positions.say: My skill's evals publish to a dashboard on every push, so anyone can check the claim.

positions.title: If I can't see what an agent did, I can't own it.
positions.body: One request to an agent becomes a tree of decisions, model calls and tool calls that nobody wrote down in advance. I want that whole tree as one connected trace, in an open format, before the agent reaches production. Cost, quality and risk all come out of the same record.
positions.say: My first note is about exactly this.

positions.title: Put the controls outside the model.
positions.body: A prompt is not a permission. Each agent gets its own identity and only the access it needs. Limits on spend and loops live in the platform, not in the instructions. People stop reading approval prompts long before an agent stops sending them, so approval can't be the only safeguard. The team that ships it stays accountable.

positions.title: Coding agents move the bottleneck. They don't remove it.
positions.body: With coding agents, writing code stops being the slow part. Deciding what to build and reviewing what comes back become the work. That makes written intent, small branches and fast checks worth more than before. It's the same discipline that keeps a team spread across time zones moving: write the decision down clearly enough that nobody has to be in the room.
positions.say: This site was built that way: several agent sessions in parallel, each on its own branch, behind a build and a link check.

lab.heading: Lab notes
lab.intro: Short and dated: what I'm testing, what I'm getting better at, and what I'd stop before it reaches production. These change more often than the rest of the site.

items.title: Problem-Based SRS
items.body: A way to write requirements that starts from the customer's problem instead of the requested feature. Paulo Cézar Stadzisz and I published it in 2016. In 2026 I turned it into an open-source agent skill for GitHub Copilot and Claude Code, so a coding agent has to trace every requirement back to a problem before it builds anything.

chain.text: Sales teams waste valuable time searching for customer information across multiple disconnected systems.

items.chainCaption: From the CRM example that ships with the skill. Each identifier names its parent, so the chain reads forward to what gets built and backward to why.

conversations.heading: Conversations
conversations.body: I'm open to conversations with teams designing or scaling agentic and AI systems. The best way to reach me is a message on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rafaelgorski).
